legend: In this problem we consider a very simplified model of Barcelona city.

Barcelona can be represented as a plane with streets of kind x=c%%ZSMJ0%% and y=c%%ZSMJ1%% for every integer c%%ZSMJ2%% (that is, the rectangular grid). However, there is a detail which makes Barcelona different from Manhattan. There is an avenue called Avinguda Diagonal which can be represented as a the set of points (x,y)%%ZSMJ3%% for which ax+by+c=0%%ZSMJ4%%.

One can walk along streets, including the avenue. You are given two integer points A%%ZSMJ5%% and B%%ZSMJ6%% somewhere in Barcelona. Find the minimal possible distance one needs to travel to get to B%%ZSMJ7%% from A%%ZSMJ8%%.
input: The first line contains three integers a%%ZSMJ9%%, b%%ZSMJ10%% and c%%ZSMJ11%% (−109≤a,b,c≤109%%ZSMJ12%%, at least one of a%%ZSMJ13%% and b%%ZSMJ14%% is not zero) representing the Diagonal Avenue.
The next line contains four integers x1%%ZSMJ15%%, y1%%ZSMJ16%%, x2%%ZSMJ17%% and y2%%ZSMJ18%% (−109≤x1,y1,x2,y2≤109%%ZSMJ19%%) denoting the points A=(x1,y1)%%ZSMJ20%% and B=(x2,y2)%%ZSMJ21%%.
output: Find the minimum possible travel distance between A%%ZSMJ22%% and B%%ZSMJ23%%. Your answer is considered correct if its absolute or relative error does not exceed 10−6%%ZSMJ24%%.
Formally, let your answer be a%%ZSMJ25%%, and the jury's answer be b%%ZSMJ26%%. Your answer is accepted if and only if |a−b|max%%ZSMJ27%%.
